\section{QB 404 examples}

% Tall QB page scans: scale below \linewidth so the unbreakable box fits the page.
\newcommand{\qbfigfit}[4]{%
  \par\needspace{18\baselineskip}%
  \begin{mdframed}[style=qbbox]
  \noindent\textbf{QB Example --- #1}\hfill Correct option:~\textbf{#2}%
  \par\smallskip
  \centering
  \includegraphics[width=0.88\linewidth,height=0.42\textheight,keepaspectratio]{#3}%
  \par\medskip
  \raggedright
  \noindent\textbf{Solution.}\quad #4
  \end{mdframed}%
}

\qbfigfit{PHY14041101--03 (p-01)}{B,\,D,\,D}{../../../_qb-assets/QB404/p-01.png}{%
\textbf{PHY14041101 (B).}
$V_{\mathrm{rms}}=I_{\mathrm{rms}}R=(5.3\times 10^{-3})(2\times 10^{3})=10.6\,\mathrm{V}$.
Peak: $V_{0}=10.6\sqrt{2}\approx 15\,\mathrm{V}$. Frequency is irrelevant.
\textbf{PHY14041102 (D).}
Same $\Delta\theta$ needs same energy $E$. With $R$ fixed,
$P\propto V^{2}$. Halving $V$ makes $P\to P/4$, so
$t=E/P\to 4\times 8=32\,\mathrm{min}$.
\textbf{PHY14041103 (D).}
$R=V_{\mathrm{r}}^{2}/P_{\mathrm{r}}=24^{2}/18=32\,\Omega$.
At $12\,\mathrm{V}$: $I_{1}=12/32=0.375\,\mathrm{A}$.
Max number: $5/0.375\approx 13.3\Rightarrow 13$ bulbs.}

Faster warming $\Rightarrow$ higher power on H: (1) true.
Supply voltage is still mains; H/L changes internal resistance/elements, not the

(3) false.
$\Rightarrow$ (1) only $\Rightarrow$ \textbf{A}.}

\begin{center}
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{2.6cm}p{11.0cm}@{}}
\toprule
Device & What it does \\
\midrule
\textbf{Fuse} &
  Sacrificial thin wire; melts on overcurrent. Cheap, one-shot; must be replaced
  with the \emph{correct} rating (never a larger fuse ``to stop nuisance blowing''). \\
\textbf{MCB} &
  Miniature circuit breaker: electromagnetic/thermal switch that trips on
  overcurrent; can be reset. Same job as a fuse (overcurrent / short / overload),
  reusable. \\
\textbf{ELCB / RCD} &
  Earth leakage / residual current device: compares current in live and neutral.
  If they differ (leakage to earth through a person or damp path), it trips
  \emph{even if the current is only tens of mA} --- far below what would blow a
  13~A fuse. Protects against shock. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
